english.title: Supply video recording - false indication for classification
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), supplied a video recording containing a video work, namely **(..SPECIFY TITLE OF VIDEO WORK..), in respect of which a classification certificate had been issued classifying the said work as **(..SPECIFY THE CLASSIFICATION TYPE..), and
(A)_[the video recording]_
(B)_[a spool on which the recording was kept]_
(C)_[a case in which the recording was kept]_
(D)_[a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY MEDIA TYPE..), on or in which the recording was kept]_

contained an indication that a classification certificate was false in a material particular as to the statements contained in it and required by Section 7(2) of the Video Recordings Act 1984 namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE FALSIFICATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 14(3) and (5) of the Video Recordings Act 1984.

english.notes:
(i) See offence wordings H3712 and H3713 for supplying video recording purporting to have a classification certificate when no such certificate had been issued.
(ii) Time limit for prosecution - either within three years of the commission of the offence of within one year of its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier (Section 15(1)).
(iii) See Section 11(1) and (2) for exemptions and defences and Sections 2 and 3 for definitions of 'exempted work' and 'exempted supply'.
(iv) See also Section 14A for general defences.
(v) See Sections 16A and 16B for extended powers of enforcing authorities and extended jurisdiction of magistrates' courts.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
